provenance.transcript:
A refrigerator moves heat out of the food compartment. A fluid called refrigerant flows through these inside coils. As it boils into gas, it absorbs heat from the air and food.

The compressor squeezes the gas, raising its pressure and temperature. It then flows through the outside coils. Here it releases heat into the room and turns back into liquid. That’s why a fridge can feel warm at the back.

Next, the liquid passes through a narrow valve. Its pressure drops, and some of it evaporates, making a cold mixture. That flows back through the inside coils to absorb more heat. The same fluid goes around again.
